# axiolid-model

Format-neutral geometry item tree. The currency between a format reader and a kernel.

## Overview

The format-neutral geometry graph that source adapters lower into and
kernels consume: an immutable, append-only DAG of typed nodes preserving
exact curves, surfaces, profiles, primitives, topology, curve and surface
relations, CSG instructions and instancing, alongside source meshes. Handles
are branded per graph and references must point to earlier nodes of the
right family, so cycles, dangling references and cross-graph handles cannot
be built. It evaluates, tessellates and compiles nothing, and keeps source
identifiers outside the graph.

The optional `serde` feature (off by default) adds the graph's versioned
wire format (ADR 0085): `GeometryGraph::to_json`, `from_json`, `to_cbor`
and `from_cbor`, and the `wire` module. Every payload names its format and
`MAJOR.MINOR` version; additions are minor versions and anything else is
major. A reader refuses by name a version it does not read, a kind,
variant or field it does not know, a non-finite number and a graph that
fails the builder's validation, and never returns part of a payload.

Default: none.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.3.12 (2026-10-13):

### Added

- Run stations at their basis's start or end, measured by the kernel
  (#303, ADR 0082 amendment): `RunStation` gains `basis_end:
  Option<BasisEnd>` (a new `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, `Start` or `End`),
  set by the constructors `RunStation::at_basis_start(offsets)` and
  `RunStation::at_basis_end(offsets)`; `None`, the default, is the stated
  `station.distance` as before. Such a station states the distance `0`,
  which is not read; a resolver reads the start as `0` and the end as the
  basis's length by the kernel's own measure. The graph refuses, as
  `GraphError::InvalidStation` when the node is pushed, a start station
  that is not the run's first, an end station that is not its last, and
  either stating a distance other than `0`; the stated distances still
  increase strictly, and whether the end comes after them is the
  resolver's check.
- Wire format 1.3 (ADR 0085 note): `RunStation.basis_end`, written only
  when it is set. A graph using it is labelled 1.3; one not using it is
  written exactly as before, as 1.0, 1.1 or 1.2. A 1.2 payload holding it
  is refused as `UnknownField` `basis_end`, by the same test the writer
  labels by. Golden payload `tests/wire/v1.3/every-kind.json`.
